title: Søren Kierkegaard's birth chart
metaDescription: Søren Kierkegaard's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.5° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 20.8° Cancer, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 14.5° into Taurus — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 25.0° Aries, Venus was at 9.2° Taurus, Mars was at 26.7° Capricorn. Read together: thought that arrives already in motion; attraction that grows by reliability; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mars sextile Uranus, 0.2° of separation. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Saturn sextile Pluto at 1.0°, and Mercury square Mars at 1.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mars opposes Jupiter while both square Mercury. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, four placements stand out. The Moon in Cancer at 20.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Taurus at 9.2° is in domicile; Mars in Capricorn at 26.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Capricorn at 19.3° is in domicile. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 earth, 3 water, 3 fire by element and 4 fixed, 4 cardinal, 2 mutable by modality. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn, Uranus and Neptune were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 20.8°.
